text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 - multi-GPU TP job hang detected. Alert: nccl_collective_deadlock. Affected job run/infra/tp-infer-9. NCCL observed 'comm abort' on rank 3 -> peer disconnect. Nodes implicated: gpu-node-134, gpu-node-135. Triggered at 2026-03-15T03:02:58Z. Paging #incidents and eng-runtime oncall.

mike: Ack, I'm oncall. Pinging @sara and @jaya for TP/NCCL help. Can someone grab pod logs and node dmesg? Hypothesis: OOM or GPU driver reset causing comm abort.

sara: grabbing logs now. I see CUDA error on gpu-node-135: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" inside the container runtime-gt-45. NCCL logs show repeated "ncclRecv: Connection reset by peer" and then comm abort. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:02:57Z] rank 3: NCCL WARN Unhandled cuda error at src/comm.c:412
[2026-03-15T03:02:58Z] rank 3: CUDA kernel abort: illegal memory access
[2026-03-15T03:03:00Z] rank 3: ncclCommAbort called
```

mike: thanks. Can you check kubelet/container status and the node dmesg for OOM or driver resets? Run `kubectl describe pod runtime-gt-45 -n runtime` and `ssh gpu-node-135 sudo dmesg | tail -n 200`.

sara: `kubectl describe` shows container state: Terminated (OOMKilled) at 03:03Z. dmesg shows an OOM kill: "Out of memory: Killed process 22456 (python)" and also a GPU driver reset entry: "nvidia: GPU reset: Xid 31". So looks like the container hit a memory limit and the driver reset followed, which explains the NCCL disconnect.

jaya: I'm on it. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nccl-hang. Immediate mitigation: isolate the offending node, restart affected containers on healthy nodes, and trigger routing fallback to single-GPU model variant for the route. We should also limit max batch size temporarily.

mike: executing node isolation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-135 && kubectl drain gpu-node-135 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Drain started at 2026-03-15T03:08:12Z.

oncall-bot: Escalation update: mike -> jaya at 2026-03-15T03:10:05Z.

frank: customer-success note: Customer A (dedicated us-west-2) reported latency spikes starting 03:04Z, ~12 failed inference requests in last 10m, some retries succeeded. Please confirm impact so we can prepare a customer message.

mike: confirmed customer impact: 12 timed-out requests, no inference outputs lost (retries hit fallback and succeeded). Marking customer impact as P1 for CS notification. Will draft a brief.

sara: restarted container runtimes on other nodes and repro'd OOM when batch size > 8 in internal test. Logs point to a potential memory regression introduced in kernel module of model-variant v1.13. Rolling back route to model:v1.12 (single-GPU) via console rollout. Example API call used: `POST /routes/route-123/rollout { \"target\": \"model:v1.12\", \"strategy\": \"immediate\" }`.

jaya: also applied temporary autoscaler throttling and batch cap (max_batch=8) for the affected route. Created INF-3021 to track root cause and driver-team coordination. Collecting core dumps from gpu-node-135 before we reprovision.

eng-sre: created incident ticket INC-4212345678 and PD alert PD-38291. Archiving logs to s3://redwood-incidents/4212345678/.

mike: short summary: mitigation in place - node drained, container restarts completed on healthy nodes, routing fallback to single-GPU model active, temporary batch cap set, customer impact limited to ~12 timed-out requests, no data loss. Handing off incident to @jaya for RCA and postmortem follow-up. My oncall shift ends in ~2h.

jaya: taking post-incident. Next actions: collect GPU core dumps, upload to S3 path above, coordinate with drivers team for Xid 31 investigation, run regression tests against model:v1.13, update runbook with a new check for container memory regressions, and prepare RCA + customer communication template.

mike: closing live coordination thread. :white_check_mark:
